trust_decision.summary: Whether a capability's value is read inside its declared CapLen is decided per capability type, in each capability's DecodeFromBytes in pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go: the shared header decode already materialises the CapLen-bounded slice as DefaultParameterCapability.CapValue, but the five fixed decoders re-slice the raw remainder of the option parameter (data = data[2:]) and check only that the whole remaining buffer is long enough, so bytes belonging to the following capability are accepted as this capability's value (AS number, AFI/SAFI, GR flags/time, FQDN names, software version).

landing_point.why: The summary names 'BGP OPEN capability parser' and 'declared CapLen boundaries', so a reader opens the OPEN option-parameter decoder; that function still knows the capability length (c.Len() = CapLen+2) but hands the entire remaining parameter buffer to DecodeCapability and then advances by CapLen, which is exactly why the leaf decoders can see bytes past their own boundary. The alternative first stop, BGPOpen.DecodeFromBytes (bgp.go:1293-1337), already slices the option parameter by ParamLen, so it looks correct on its face.

fix_sites.entry_point: bgp.ParseBGPBody from a live BGP session (pkg/server/fsm.go:1312) -> BGPOpen.DecodeFromBytes (bgp.go:1293) -> OptionParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes (bgp.go:1227) -> DecodeCapability (bgp.go:1178); also bgp.ParseBGPMessage from BMP peer-up OPENs (pkg/packet/bmp/bmp.go:567,573) and MRT BGP4MP messages (pkg/packet/mrt/mrt.go:890); also a direct library call to (*CapMultiProtocol).DecodeFromBytes
fix_sites.module_kind: packet codec, exported DecodeFromBytes method on a public capability type (pkg/packet/bgp)

fix_sites.entry_point: same OPEN path; (*CapGracefulRestart).DecodeFromBytes via DecodeCapability (bgp.go:1193) or called directly (as pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:4522 already does)

same OPEN path; (*CapFourOctetASNumber).DecodeFromBytes via DecodeCapability (bgp.go:1195); its value becomes the peer AS used by ValidateOpenMsg (pkg/packet/bgp/validate.go:292-295) and getASN (pkg/server/fsm.go:592-596)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go:503-513, and the same lower-level site in the other four fixed decoders (bgp.go:684-712, 765-775, 1032-1066, 1116-1131)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once the OPEN parser bounds each capability slice in OptionParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes, the exported per-type DecodeFromBytes methods are only reached through that one wrapper, so a solver can argue the leaf decoders need no length check of their own - which is false for library callers and for the project's own FuzzDecodeFromBytes, which calls each capability's DecodeFromBytes directly (pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:4519-4527).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: One capability option parameter legitimately carries several capabilities, so the buffer handed to each leaf decoder extends past 2+CapLen and must still be accepted; a fix that requires len(data) to equal 2+CapLen (or that rejects trailing bytes) breaks every normal multi-capability OPEN, such as the one in Test_BGPOpenDecodeCapabilities (pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:4430-4456) which packs extended-nexthop, add-path and long-lived-graceful-restart into a single parameter. Also CapLen==2 for graceful restart (no AFI/SAFI tuples) is legal and gobgp's own encoder emits it whenever Tuples is empty (bgp.go:714-726), so a fix demanding at least one tuple breaks it.

O6_input_shapes: CapLen=0 with the following capability's bytes present in the same option parameter (value absent, bytes available)
CapLen shorter than the fixed-size value (1 or 2 for multiprotocol / four-octet-AS)
CapLen longer than the fixed-size value (e.g. 5 for multiprotocol or four-octet-AS, so the extra byte must not be read)
capability that is the last one in the parameter, so the buffer ends exactly at 2+CapLen
capability followed by one or more further capabilities, so the buffer is longer than 2+CapLen
inner length fields that exceed CapLen but fit the remaining buffer (FQDN host-name/domain-name length bytes at bgp.go:1045-1064, software-version length byte at bgp.go:1124-1129)
graceful restart CapLen of 2 (flags+time only) and of 2+4n with tuples

O7_producer.where: pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go:470-483 (DefaultParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes is the shared header/value deserialiser that materialises the CapLen-bounded CapValue slice at bgp.go:480, which the fix consumes; every leaf decoder calls it and then ignores its output)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a decoder for a capability code that gobgp does not implement yet (ORF 3, Extended Message 6, BGP Role 9) that re-slices data[2:] and reads a fixed-size value, exactly like the five fixed ones
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DecodeCapability is a one-branch-per-code switch and five of its branches were written with that mistake; unimplemented codes currently fall through to CapUnknown, so adding a typed capability is a routine contribution that reproduces the bug.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: BMP information TLV values parsed from the whole remaining buffer (ParseValue(data) at bmp.go:730) instead of data[:tl.Length], the same declared-length-ignored pattern one package away
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseBMPInfoTLVs already checks len(data) >= tl.Length (bmp.go:720-722) and then passes the unbounded slice to ParseValue; this is the same authoring habit the capability decoders show, so a sibling written in that style is plausible and already exists for TLVs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a typed decoder for a second OPEN optional-parameter type (the switch handles only BGP_OPT_CAPABILITY; other types fall to OptionParameterUnknown at bgp.go:1267-1282) that reads its value from the full remainder instead of data[2:2+paramlen]
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BGPOpen.DecodeFromBytes already bounds capability parameters by ParamLen at bgp.go:1313-1323; a maintainer adding a typed parameter would add a case next to that branch and could easily read from data without re-applying the ParamLen slice.

O9_family: out-of-bounds read of a length-delimited protocol field (CWE-125) in a BGP OPEN capability parser; declared-length boundary not enforced before decoding a capability value

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.24.5 (go.mod:3), Go modules with no vendor directory; go build ./... ; go test ./pkg/packet/bgp/... needs no cgo, no root and no network
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:1711 TestCapSoftwareVersionRoundTrip, :1726 TestFuzzCrashers (seed strings through ParseBGPMessage), :4430 Test_BGPOpenDecodeCapabilities (full OPEN message with several capabilities in one parameter), :4492 FuzzParseBGPMessage, :4508 FuzzDecodeFromBytes (calls every capability DecodeFromBytes directly at :4519-4527); there is no test at the pinned commit that varies CapLen against the buffer length

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound the slice once in OptionParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes / DecodeCapability (data[:2+int(data[1])]) instead of reading each value from the CapLen-bounded DefaultParameterCapability.CapValue, which passes a message-level test while the exported per-type DecodeFromBytes methods still read past CapLen.

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/packet/bmp/bmp.go:720-734 parseBMPInfoTLVs passes the unbounded remaining buffer to tlv.ParseValue after checking only len(data) >= Length - the same declared-length-ignored mechanism, but in the BMP parser, not the BGP OPEN capability parser this advisory covers; not pursued.

The pinned tree already enforces the boundary in CapExtendedNexthop (bgp.go:600-615), CapAddPath (bgp.go:859-873) and CapLongLivedGracefulRestart (bgp.go:974-988), and path attributes get a bounded value back from PathAttribute.DecodeFromBytes (bgp.go:11196); these were read only to establish that no route into the same sink is left unprotected.
